title: Conditions of Hire: Damage, Cleaning, Tolls and Fines Recharged After Return
content:
**1. What is recharged.** Damage discovered at return or afterwards is recharged to the renter up to the rate class's waiver excess where the waiver was carried, and in full where it was not.

**2. The state the rental must stand in.** A recharge is raised only while the rental record stands at picked up or returned.

**3. The assessment.** Damage is recharged only when the rental desk has already recorded an approved damage assessment against this rental.

**4. The reporting window.** Damage found after the vehicle was handed back is recharged only when frozen time is not after the moment the renter returned the vehicle to the supplier plus the damage reporting window of the rate class booked. The damage reporting window is counted in whole calendar days from the day after the return date, weekends and public holidays included, and a report made exactly on the closing day is still in time.

**5. Administration.** The class's damage administration charge is added once per incident and never once per damaged part.

**6. Tolls and fines.** Tolls and traffic fines incurred during the rental are recharged at the amount the authority charged plus the class's own administration charge for each toll or each fine.

**7. Soiling and smoking.** Excessive soiling and smoking in the vehicle carry the class's own charges and are settled as recharges rather than as damage.

**8. A disputed recharge.** A renter who disputes a recharge is referred to a review, and the disputed amount stays on the ledger until the review decides it.

**The three conditions that must hold together.** Before damage is recharged on the Car Rental Rate Classes, the rental record must stand at picked up or returned; an approved damage assessment must already stand recorded by the rental desk against this rental, identified by the assessment's own reference; and, where the damage was found after the vehicle was handed back, frozen time must be not after the return moment plus the class's reporting window. Each of the three rests on the company's own records rather than on what the renter or the supplier says, and each is read before the recharge is raised.

**The window, counted on hypothetical dates.** The window runs in whole calendar days beginning the day after the return date, and weekends and public holidays are counted like any other day. On a class publishing a window of 7 calendar days, a vehicle returned on a given date leaves the window open through the seventh day after it: a report made on that seventh day is exactly on the closing day and is still in time, while a report on the eighth day is out of time. On a class publishing 14 calendar days the same counting reaches the fourteenth day after the return date.

**How far the recharge goes.** Where the waiver was carried on the rental, the recharge reaches no further than the class's waiver excess. Where it was not carried, the damage is recharged in full. Either way the class's damage administration charge is added once for the incident, however many parts of the vehicle the incident touched.
